clue.text: Silly old lady and current old man coming back

parts.note: an old lady is slang for one's mother
direct current, abbreviated

indicators.note: something coming back travels the opposite way, so this word is read from right to left

parts.note: an old man is slang for one's father

explanation.surface: A daft elderly couple, one of them returning from somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: MA + DC + AP (PA backwards) gives MADCAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap scheme or person is wildly foolish, a lively synonym for silly.

clue.text: Enthusiastic duck? No, not duck

indicators.note: saying no to something and doing without it tells you to take it out of the word

parts.note: to duck a question is to dodge it
a duck in cricket is a score of zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone keen asks whether to dodge, then is told not to.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word is used twice in two senses: the verb meaning dodge, then the cricket zero. AVOID without its O leaves AVID.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or keen, so it is a straight synonym for enthusiastic.

clue.text: Hole in rocklike material — concrete?

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, splitting the outer word

parts.note: coral is the hard, stony material of reefs
a pore is a tiny hole, as in skin

explanation.surface: A query about whether a cavity in some stony stuff is concrete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concrete' looks like the building material, continuing the stone theme, but it is the adjective meaning tangible. PORE goes into COR|AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporeal means having a physical body, so it is something real and tangible rather than abstract.

clue.text: Suddenly new city (as of 2002)

parts.note: presto, as in a conjuror's 'hey presto', means all of a sudden
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A town abruptly becomes a brand-new city in a particular year.
explanation.walkthrough: Preston, in Lancashire in north-west England, was granted city status in 2002 for the Queen's Golden Jubilee, so the surface is literally true.
explanation.definitionFit: Preston is an English town that was made a city in 2002, so the bracketed date pins it down.

clue.text: Dilute the fruit regularly through cleaning

indicators.note: running through something places these letters inside the other word

parts.note: a wash is a cleaning

indicators.note: doing something regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: letters one, three, five and seven of these two words

explanation.surface: An instruction to thin down the fruit by washing it repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dilute' looks like a verb opening an instruction, but it is the adjective meaning watered down.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterish describes something watered down or thin, the adjectival sense of dilute.

clue.text: Before income tax, this is what police heard about

definitions.meaning: first meaning: on the British Monopoly board this street comes just before the Income Tax square
second meaning: the East London street where the Jack the Ripper murders were reported to police

explanation.surface: Something that precedes paying tax, and which the police received reports of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before income tax' reads like gross pay, but it means position on a Monopoly board, the property game whose British edition uses London streets.
explanation.definitionFit: The street sits second on the British Monopoly board, just ahead of Income Tax, and was the scene of notorious crimes.

clue.text: Petty criminal may be up for it — sex in custody

indicators.note: someone in custody is held inside, so these letters are enclosed by the other word

parts.words: criminal may be up for it
parts.note: a criminal may be up for trial
sex is Latin for six, VI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A minor offender facing charges, with a sexual element held over him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex' is not about sex but the Latin word for six, written in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty and trivial both mean small and unimportant, so they are straight synonyms.

clue.text: Blue? No time to talk

indicators.note: having no time means the time abbreviation is dropped from the word

parts.note: to rabbit on is British slang for talking at length
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Feeling down, with no time to chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like sadness but is Lionel Blue, a well-known British rabbi and broadcaster; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lionel Blue was a famous Reform rabbi heard on BBC radio, so he is an example of a rabbi.

clue.text: Copper comes in to arrest different relative

indicators.note: coming in to something means entering it, so this letter goes inside the next word

parts.note: to stem is to arrest or stop a flow
a copper is a penny coin, P
other means different

explanation.surface: A police officer arrives to detain a different family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' and 'arrest' suggest the police, but the copper is a penny, and to arrest is to stop a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepmother is a relative by marriage, a father's wife who is not the birth mother.

clue.text: Old PM is with artist opening shop

indicators.note: opening something up lets these letters in, so they sit inside the following word

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen shop
taken as written
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A former prime minister and a painter start up a shop together.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian British prime minister, so he is an old PM.

clue.text: I notice colour associated with Indian native

parts.note: taken as written
NB, nota bene, means take notice
Indian red is a shade of reddish-brown pigment

explanation.surface: Someone spots a colour linked with an indigenous person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian native' reads as a phrase, but 'Indian' belongs with the colour and 'native' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Inbred can mean innate, inborn or natural to someone, the adjectival sense of native.

clue.text: Promised time off in the afternoon

indicators.note: something off has gone wrong or bad, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone was promised an afternoon off work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' sits naturally as time off, but it signals the letters are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Post meridiem is the Latin phrase behind p.m., meaning after midday.

clue.text: Endless praise has church make a fresh start

indicators.note: something without an end loses its final letter

parts.note: to recommend someone is to praise them
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Unceasing worship lets a congregation begin anew.
explanation.walkthrough: RECOMMEND loses its last letter, then CE is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To recommence is to begin again, which is to make a fresh start.

clue.text: River runs through rabbi's location

indicators.note: something running through another passes inside it

parts.note: the rabbi is the answer at 7 down, so his location in the grid is seven
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A river flows past a rabbi's home.
explanation.walkthrough: This refers across the grid: the rabbi is the answer at 7 down. R goes inside SEVE|N.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn is Britain's longest river, flowing from Wales through England to the Bristol Channel.

clue.text: Absence of gravity, or term describing it

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round, so the term goes round the next word

parts.note: Hilary term is the spring term at Oxford and in the law courts
taken as written

explanation.surface: A frivolous mood, or the word one uses for weightlessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing round, as one describes a circle; 'gravity' means seriousness, not the physical force.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilarity is uproarious merriment, the opposite of gravity in the sense of seriousness.

clue.text: Trucker Eddie's elected to carry fuel

indicators.note: the words carry the answer inside them, holding it within their run of letters

parts.note: found inside these words, from the second letter of the first

explanation.surface: A lorry driver is voted in to haul fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer starts in tRucker and runs through Eddie's into ELected. Red diesel is cheap dyed fuel restricted in Britain to farm and off-road vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Red diesel is a tax-reduced diesel dyed red, a type of fuel.

clue.text: Sweet lozenge turned into circular shape

indicators.note: put into something means placed inside it

parts.note: a loop is a circular shape

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lozenge is a small medicinal tablet or pill

explanation.surface: A boiled sweet is twisted into a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' could be an adjective, but it is the confectionery noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a sweet on a stick, a type of confectionery.

clue.text: Secretary's learned to make progress

parts.note: a PA is a personal assistant; the possessive adds S
a sage person is learned and wise

explanation.surface: An assistant has studied in order to get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learned' looks like a past-tense verb but is the adjective meaning wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Passage means movement onward through time or space, as in the passage of years, a sense of progress.

clue.text: Cheap beer, see?

parts.note: Bud is short for Budweiser, a brand of beer
to see a point is to get it; 'get it?' means 'see?'

explanation.surface: Pointing out to someone how inexpensive the beer is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See?' reads as a tag question but means understand.
explanation.definitionFit: A budget product or airline is a low-cost one, so budget works as an adjective for cheap.

clue.text: Small sphere or circle?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ball ..., the small steel ball in a machine
second meaning: a heraldic charge on a shield, of which a roundel or ring is an example

explanation.walkthrough: Both definitions sound like geometry; the question mark marks the second as an example of a heraldic device.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball bearing is a little steel ball, and in heraldry any charge such as a circle is a bearing.

clue.text: You and I are barely talking

definitions.text: You and I are barely talking

parts.words: You and I are barely talking
parts.note: surface reading: two people who have fallen out and hardly speak
setter's reading: the words you, and, I and are each have one syllable, and someone barely talking speaks in such curt words

explanation.surface: Two people are hardly on speaking terms after a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The words of the clue itself are all one-syllable words, which is also how a terse speaker talks.
explanation.definitionFit: A monosyllabic reply is curt, words of one syllable from someone who will hardly talk.

clue.text: Close to — halfway there — death?

parts.note: nigh means near or close to

indicators.note: going only halfway means just a part of the word is taken, its leading letter

parts.note: the start of this word

explanation.surface: Someone near the end is partway along the road to dying.
explanation.walkthrough: Death is poetically called the long night, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is a poetic image for death, the darkness that ends life, so it fits by figurative extension.

clue.text: Type of cable, about 57% flatter

indicators.note: roughly fifty-seven per cent of a seven-letter word is four letters, so the rest is cut off

parts.note: coaxial cable is the shielded kind used for TV aerials

explanation.surface: A cable type described as somewhat more level.
explanation.walkthrough: Four of seven letters is 57.1%, hence 'about'. 'Flatter' looks like a comparative of flat but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax someone is to persuade them with gentle words, close in sense to flattering them.

clue.text: Imagine not starting cryptic puzzle

indicators.note: a word not starting has lost its first letter
something cryptic is obscured and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word minus its first letter

explanation.surface: An invitation to picture a crossword with no obvious way in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic puzzle' reads as a crossword, but 'cryptic' is the mixing signal and 'puzzle' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or riddle, a synonym for puzzle.

clue.text: It may create space over goal

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a mission is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Something that might open up room above the target, as in football.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space over goal' sounds like football tactics, but it is a gap left by leaving something out.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving something out of a text creates a gap, so an omission produces empty space.

clue.text: Drink bottles use up hot sap

indicators.note: a drink that bottles something holds it inside, so the other letters are enclosed

parts.note: mead is a drink made from honey
to eat up resources is to consume them
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Mead bottling consumes hot tree juice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sap' looks like tree juice but is a fool, a gullible person.
explanation.definitionFit: A meathead is a stupid person, the same informal sense as sap meaning a gullible fool.

clue.text: Many stars possibly camp outside American airport

indicators.note: placing one word outside another wraps it around

parts.note: camp and gay can both mean flamboyant or homosexual
LAX is the code for Los Angeles International Airport

explanation.surface: Lots of celebrities might be found camping near a US airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' suggests Hollywood celebrities near Los Angeles, but it means stars in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A galaxy is a vast system of billions of stars; possibly marks a definition by description.
